context_documents.title: 2023-1727 · Direct acquisition keeps the subsystem count low but makes reach geometry decisive
context_documents.body:
# 2023-1727: Direct acquisition keeps the subsystem count low but makes reach geometry decisive

Focused study supplement. Not a full binder/CAD review, exhaustive subsystem specification, every-version history or visual interview watch.

## Published / retained construction account

A swerve chassis carries an arm with an extending elevator and end roller collector, acquiring directly from the floor and single substation and reaching all grid levels. No independent transfer mechanism is established in the reviewed passage.

## Team-stated reasoning or boundary

The team explicitly seeks a simple, robust, efficient robot and identifies this as its first competition season using swerve. The caption’s combined module/gearing terminology needs a hardware check before treating it as a part specification.

## Engineering interpretation — analyst inference

Direct pickup removes a handoff, but reach, wrist attitude and ground clearance must all be solved by the scoring mechanism. A successful demonstration at one field location does not prove access to every node with realistic partner traffic. First-year swerve readiness also consumes tuning and practice capacity that belongs in the design decision.

## Proposed validation — not performed

Map all required approach poses, measure acquisition tolerance, and test full extension with each piece under chassis motion. Leave undisclosed transmission details unresolved.

## Limits

Focused technical passages and the retained dossier are the evidence scope. Exact event installation, complete CAD tolerances and all intermediate revisions are not certified.

## Sources and navigation

- [https://youtu.be/6OCIr35tAi0](https://youtu.be/6OCIr35tAi0)

binder_audit.interpretation: A missing verified binder is an unresolved retrieval result, not evidence the team never published one. Existing interviews/CAD sources remain usable.

source_reviews.title: REX 2023 FIRST Charged Up Technical Binder
source_reviews.locator: Printed pp. 4–14, especially Arm p. 8, Elevator p. 9 and Intake p. 10
source_reviews.review_basis: Read team binder text and labeled drawing text on p. 6 through the web tool.
source_reviews.facts: The binder identifies the drivetrain, a rotating arm and two-stage lift, the direct compliant roller intake, low-mounted electronics and scoring poses.
source_reviews.limitations: The double substation is a design objective. The capability discussion names floor and single-substation collection. Free drive speed is a published estimate. The binder does not assign hardware to individual matches.

source_review.whole_robot_explanation: Incline uses a rotating support arm and telescoping lift to position a single side-roller head for both collection and scoring. The team describes the controls as polar coordinates. The arm sets angle and the elevator sets reach, so those axes can move together without asking the driver to reposition the chassis for every change in height. REX's game analysis called for a robot that could create links and engage with limited help. Direct acquisition, a low chassis and preselected geometry address different parts of that goal.
source_review.piece_flow: For floor or single-substation collection, the arm and elevator bring the roller head to the piece. Mixed-durometer wheels deform around cones and around cubes whose inflation varies. The same head retains the piece while the two positioning axes change angle and reach and presents it at the intended node for outtake. There is no separate transfer in the documented path. The binder reports less than 90 degrees of arm movement and over three feet of lift extension. It does not specify the complete release-direction or roller-current schedule.
source_review.packaging_and_motion: The arm turns about a dead axle also used in powering the elevator, with a modular connection between assemblies. The sponsor panel doubles as lift protection and a cable-chain track. REX locates ballast inside three drive rails and the battery horizontally over the belly pan. Inference: on extended poses, stability depends on horizontal offset and chassis acceleration as much as on lift height. Check the swept polycarbonate head and cable chain between presets, especially when leaving ground pickup with a piece retained.

subsystems.name: Swerve and base
subsystems.construction: 24 by 28 inch aluminum MaxTube chassis with REV MAXSwerve, four NEO 1.1 drive motors and four NEO 550 steering motors. Drive reduction is 5.08:1. A 1/8-inch aluminum belly pan and 15 lb of steel rail ballast sit low.
subsystems.operation: Independent steering permits translation around obstacles and a wheel-lock configuration for station use.
subsystems.team_rationale: REX sought strafe mobility and a low center of gravity. Toggle clamps are specified for rapid bumper swaps.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Test downhill braking and direction reversals with a representative high extension, where wheel load transfer can undermine pose control.
subsystems.interfaces: Arm and ballast loads enter the frame. The belly pan protects and carries electronics.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Inspect clamps, wheel steering zero and rail retention after hard impacts.
subsystems.unknowns: Loaded speed and measured stability margin.

subsystems.name: Arm and telescope
subsystems.construction: Arm uses one NEO 1.1 with 100:1 MaxPlanetary and two 30 lb gas springs. A turnbuckle adjusts the fixed-center chain. The two-stage Thrifty Bot lift uses custom string and pulleys, a 9:1 planetary and a 2:1 external gear stage.
subsystems.operation: The two axes can travel simultaneously to a preset. The shared axle and removable lift attachment integrate the drives.
subsystems.team_rationale: REX cites shorter piece transit and straightforward removal of the arm from the elevator.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Gas assist varies with geometry. Check shoulder tracking across extension because both gravity leverage and reflected inertia change.
subsystems.interfaces: Shared axle, lift mount, string path and protected cable chain all cross the pivot-to-extension boundary.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Check string tracking and tension, chain slack and spring mounts before retuning. Confirm the lift can be removed without losing alignment.
subsystems.unknowns: String anchoring and event-specific tension settings.

subsystems.name: Roller head and controls
subsystems.construction: Six four-inch VEXpro flex wheels, four 30A and two 45A, in quarter-inch polycarbonate. One NEO drives the head. Lift and arm use PID position control.
subsystems.operation: Preset scoring poses coordinate both axes. PathPlanner event markers run subsystem commands during autonomous travel.
subsystems.team_rationale: The team prioritized positive capture despite variable piece compliance and reduced driver input.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: A failed grab ties up the scoring axes. Measure acquisition tolerance in yaw, height and piece deformation before extending the concept to crowded approaches.
subsystems.interfaces: Head rides the moving lift. Electrical leads must traverse the pivot and the extension track.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Check polycarbonate hole elongation, wheel wear, wire strain and whether an interrupted preset can be recovered cleanly.
subsystems.unknowns: Exact head reduction convention and acquisition confirmation method.

revisions: The team reports changing from difficult-to-service inverted electronics on an earlier robot to a topside belly-pan layout. The binder also reports upgrading battery leads from 6 to 4 AWG with right-angle fastening. No dated 2023 manipulator swaps were established.
transferable_principles: Design pickup and placement as a common pose map when one head can retain both pieces. Use the protective panel as a defined wiring surface if cable motion can be inspected.
disconfirming_conditions: The direct path loses its benefit if bumpers or field lips force repeated realignment, a held piece obstructs retraction, or combined axis motion consumes the available stability margin.
remaining_gaps: End-of-travel and recovery behavior in deployed code, double-substation coverage, measured cycle times, and exact as-competed configurations.

recommended_images.subject: Overview, pivot/lift interface, mixed-wheel head and electrical layout. Caption the depicted configuration and mark the shared axle and moving harness.
